title: Information Technology Modernization Centers of Excellence Program Act
official_summary:
Information Technology Modernization Centers of Excellence Program Act

This bill requires the General Services Administration (GSA) to establish an Information Technology Modernization Centers of Excellence Program to facilitate the adoption of modern technology by executive agencies.

The GSA shall (1) coordinate with the Department of Homeland Security in establishing the program to ensure that the technology, tools, and frameworks facilitated for executive agencies by the program provide sufficient cybersecurity and maintain the integrity, confidentiality, and availability of federal information; and (2) report to Congress.

summary.headline: This law requires the General Services Administration to set up a program that helps federal agencies adopt modern technology while keeping cybersecurity in mind.
summary.what_it_does: The law directs the General Services Administration (GSA) to create an Information Technology Modernization Centers of Excellence Program. The program is meant to help executive branch agencies adopt newer technology. GSA must work with the Department of Homeland Security so that the tools and frameworks provided include adequate cybersecurity and protect the integrity, confidentiality, and availability of federal information. GSA must also report to Congress.

who_it_affects.how: Agencies may receive technology, tools, and frameworks through the new program to help them modernize their information systems.
Staff who manage agency technology may work with tools and frameworks that the program makes available and must meet the cybersecurity goals the program sets.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the public who use federal services
who_it_affects.how: The program aims to protect the security and reliability of federal information systems that hold their data, though the summary does not describe direct changes to individual services.
